A Bulldog in the adult chapter is not a generic dog. For this Bulldog, adult weight lands around 40-50 lb (18-23 kg), lifespan is typically 8-10 years, and day-to-day temperament looks like this: Calm companion; limited exercise tolerance; avoid heat and overexertion. This Bulldog adult guide focuses on weight discipline, dental rhythm, and steady monitoring for Brachycephalic obstructive airway syndrome (BOAS) and Hip dysplasia. ## What normal looks like for a adult Bulldog

Adult Bulldogs should keep a palpable rib grid under that coat. Looking "like a Bulldog" is not a body condition score. For this Bulldog, exercise should match this temperament note without turning a weekend into an ER visit: Calm companion; limited exercise tolerance; avoid heat and overexertion. Dental home care belongs on the same calendar as vaccines for a Bulldog expected to live 8-10 years. For this Bulldog, grooming is also a medical pass: Daily fold cleaning; short coat, low brush need. Keep certificates, weights, and meds in one vault so boarding desks stop inventing a Bulldog history from texts. For this Bulldog, adult monitoring for Brachycephalic obstructive airway syndrome (BOAS) and Hip dysplasia is mostly boring consistency: same scale, same walking surface, same weekly glance at appetite and stool. ## Breed-linked issues to watch in this stage

In an adult Bulldog, Brachycephalic obstructive airway syndrome (BOAS) is managed with boring monthly checks rather than crisis-only attention. Keep a Bulldog log with date, what you saw, and a photo if useful. For this Bulldog, escalation cues for Brachycephalic obstructive airway syndrome (BOAS) are on /symptoms/difficulty-breathing-dog. In an adult Bulldog, Hip dysplasia is managed with boring monthly checks rather than crisis-only attention. Home monitoring for this Bulldog means dating exercise tolerance, pain signs, breathing effort, itch, or litter changes. For this Bulldog, red flags belong on /symptoms/limping-dog before a forum thread. In an adult Bulldog, Cherry eye is managed with boring monthly checks rather than crisis-only attention. Matching signs should send a Bulldog caregiver to /symptoms/red-eyes-dog for urgency framing, then to the clinic with the written timeline. ## Practical context for this Bulldog

Temperament shapes adult-stage risk management for a Bulldog: Calm companion; limited exercise tolerance; avoid heat and overexertion. For this Bulldog, copied exercise advice from another breed fails this medium animal in the adult chapter. Lifespan expectations around 8-10 years change how early a Bulldog household starts screening talks for Brachycephalic obstructive airway syndrome (BOAS) during adult care. Adult travel is where Bulldog paperwork dies. For this Bulldog, photograph certificates the day they are issued for this adult packet. ## Home-monitoring checklist

Use this Bulldog adult monitoring list weekly. For this Bulldog, if an item fails twice in a row, write it down and tell the veterinarian:

1. Weigh the Bulldog on the same scale. For this Bulldog, keep adult awareness around 40-50 lb (18-23 kg), or a smooth curve if still growing. 2. For this Bulldog, scan for Brachycephalic obstructive airway syndrome (BOAS) clues first: gait, breathing effort, itch, appetite, stool, or litter and urine changes. 3. For this Bulldog, add a second pass for Hip dysplasia so two breed risks are not competing for the same glance. 4. Do a sixty-second coat and skin check while grooming this Bulldog. For this Bulldog, grooming note: Daily fold cleaning; short coat, low brush need. 5. Confirm parasite prevention dates for this Bulldog are real dates, not vibes. 6. Update the vaccine and visit packet so the next boarding desk or ER sees the actual Bulldog history. 7. Check that sitters can open your Bulldog share link on airplane mode before you leave town. None of this replaces a veterinarian who knows your Bulldog. For this Bulldog, it keeps the adult story coherent between visits so early disease is harder to miss.

faqs.question: What is a normal adult weight range for a Bulldog?
faqs.answer: This breed record lists 40-50 lb (18-23 kg). Your veterinarian sets the target for the individual using body condition, not only the breed average.

faqs.question: Which health issues should I watch for in a adult Bulldog?
faqs.answer: This stage guide highlights Brachycephalic obstructive airway syndrome (BOAS); Hip dysplasia; Cherry eye. Use the linked symptom pages for red flags, then contact your clinic.

faqs.question: How often should I weigh my Bulldog at this stage?
faqs.answer: Every 30 days is a practical adult Bulldog default unless your veterinarian sets a tighter plan.
